claims.text: Corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection in Q235 steel is primarily governed by the formation and stability of a protective oxide layer.
Temperature influences the formation and stability of the protective oxide layer on Q235 steel.
Aggressive salt exposure conditions influence the formation and stability of the protective oxide layer on Q235 steel.
The state of the protective oxide layer leads to either corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection.
The proposed study will vary temperature systematically from 25 to 900 °C.
The proposed study will vary aggressive salt concentration from 0% to 10%.
Relative to Q235 steel exposed to aggressive salt at room temperature, exposure at 700 °C will produce a 20% reduction in mass change.
Relative to Q235 steel exposed to aggressive salt at room temperature, exposure at 900 °C will produce a 30% increase in mass change.
The hypothesis applies to Q235 steel between 25 and 900 °C and at aggressive salt concentrations from 0% to 10%.
The hypothesis does not apply outside the specified temperature or salt-concentration ranges.
The hypothesis does not apply to types of steel other than Q235.
Other corrosive substances may influence corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection in Q235 steel.
The microstructure of Q235 steel may influence its corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection.
The hypothesis will be rejected if the mass change at 700 °C is not within 10% of the predicted value.
The hypothesis will be rejected if microstructural analysis does not show the expected formation and stability of the protective oxide layer.
